item.title: Thank you.
item.description:
Good Morning,

Thank you for participating in the Mayoral Leadership In Education Network (MLEN) data dashboard stakeholders meeting on December 10 with the Workforce Development Board of Central Ohio and Emsi.  I hope you were inspired by the demonstration and excited about how you can use the tools to assist both your organization and our disadvantaged youth.
 
You should have received an email from Hector Acosta with Emsi asking you to identify the specific individuals within your organization who will use the data. Emsi will be leading training sessions at 11 am on Thursday, January 21 and Wednesday, January 27.  These training sessions will be more technical and should be attended by the identified data-users from your organization.
 
If you have not already responded to Hector with this information please do so.
 
Thank you again for your participation in this important project and your work in our community.

item.title: You're Invited!
item.description:
Greetings,

The City of Columbus and the Workforce Development Board of Central Ohio are engaged in an education to workforce pipeline pilot project with the Mayoral Leadership In Education Network (MLEN) at the Harvard Kennedy School.  This work, led by former Indianapolis Mayor Stephen Goldsmith and funded through a grant from the Strada Education Network and the United Negro College Fund (UNCF), is focused on providing skills and opportunities to disadvantaged youth.

Using EMSI data, MLEN is developing two dashboards, proprietary to Columbus that educators, employers, and policy makers can use to identify needs and opportunities and make strategic decisions in real time. 

By extrapolating demand-side skills data from regional job postings, one dashboard identifies what specific skills are needed by employers, and what training should be applied.  Advocates and community leaders who work with disadvantaged youth can use this data to help individuals acquire training and move to better-paying jobs.  In addition, this dashboard could be used to assist youth with important decision making regarding their future career paths and post-secondary education.

The second dashboard helps regional planners identify what skills and talents are abundant and available.  This data could then be used to prioritize the development of businesses in the area or incentivize the relocation of companies seeking a skilled workforce.

Through the grant we are provided with 30 access points to the dashboards.  You and your organization have been identified as a critical partner in this work and we invite you to participate. 

I would like to invite you to attend a virtual, introductory meeting on Thursday, December 10 at 4 pm.  MLEN and UNCF will walk us through the data and how it can be used.
